headline: 14 killed in bus-truck collision in Natore
summary: A head-on crash between a Rajshahi-bound bus and a sand-laden truck left at least 14 dead and over 20 injured near Bonpara.
details: At least 14 people were killed and more than 20 others injured in a head-on collision between a bus and a truck on the Pabna-Natore highway near Bonpara early today.
A Rajshahi-bound RP Paribahan bus collided with a sand-laden truck around 4:00 am, according to Sub-Inspector Md Alamgir Hossain of the Bonpara Highway Police Station.

Police and firefighters rushed to the scene to conduct rescue operations, while the injured were transported to Natore General Hospital, the Boraigram Upazila Health Complex, and other nearby facilities.
Natore Superintendent of Police Md Shariful Haque confirmed the death toll and stated that an investigation into the incident is underway.
A seven-member probe committee, headed by Additional District Magistrate Abul Hayat, has been formed to investigate the cause of the accident.
The collision disrupted vehicular movement on the Pabna-Rajshahi highway for several hours.

headline: Around 50 vehicles robbed by armed gang on Cox’s Bazar road
summary: Masked gunmen intercepted motorcycles and autorickshaws, looting cash and valuables at gunpoint before fleeing into the forest.
details: Around 50 vehicles were robbed in two separate incidents on the Eidgaon-Eidghar-Baishari road in Cox’s Bazar yesterday afternoon.
A group of 10 to 12 masked men armed with weapons blocked the road at Himchhari Dhala, intercepting CNG-run autorickshaws and motorcycles.
Victims reported being held hostage at gunpoint, with some being taken to a nearby forest and beaten before their cash, mobile phones, and valuables were stolen.
One victim, a manager of a private organisation, reported losing Tk 1.2 lakh, while another accountant lost Tk 1.5 lakh during the robberies.
Eidgaon Police Station Officer-in-Charge ATM Shifatul Majdar confirmed the incidents and stated that the robbers fled into the forest after the loot.
Police have launched operations and stepped up patrols in the hilly areas of Ramu and Eidgaon upazilas to arrest the suspects, though no one has been detained yet.
Local residents noted that robberies and abductions are frequent on this 17-kilometre hilly road, leading many to stop traveling after dusk due to security concerns.

Eidgaon Police Station Officer-in-Charge ATM Shifatul Majdar confirmed the incidents and stated that the robbers fled into the forest after the loot.

Police have launched operations and stepped up patrols in the hilly areas of Ramu and Eidgaon upazilas to arrest the suspects, though no one has been detained yet.
